name: ACS733KLATR-40AB-T
title: ACS732 and ACS733: 1 MHz isolated Hall-effect current sensor with overcurrent fault, SOICW-16
summary: A Hall-effect current sensor with an internal 1 mΩ copper current path on pins 1 to 8, galvanically isolated from the sensing IC on pins 9 to 16. The analog output follows AC or DC current with 1 MHz bandwidth and is ratiometric to the supply; an open-drain FAULT output flags overcurrent at a threshold set by a resistor divider on VOC. ACS732 variants run from 5 V and ACS733 variants from 3.3 V, in ranges of 20 A to 75 A, bidirectional or unidirectional. ACS733KLATR-40AB-T is the 3.3 V, ±40 A bidirectional part at 33 mV/A.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: The current to be measured enters at IP+ (pins 1 to 4) and leaves at IP- (pins 5 to 8), on the isolated side of the package. The low-voltage side runs from VCC with CBYPASS from VCC to ground. A two-resistor divider from VCC to ground sets the VOC voltage, which sets the overcurrent threshold IFAULT; resistors under 10 kΩ keep the VOC leakage from moving the trip point. RF(PULLUP) pulls the open-drain FAULT output up to VCC. VIOUT carries the analog output, loaded by CL to ground. PROGRAM and both GND pins go to ground.

notes: The divider ratio picks IFAULT: VVOC = (VCC / 5) × IFAULT / IPR(MAX), with VVOC from 0.1 × VCC to 0.4 × VCC.

operation.text: Current through the internal copper path, about 1 mΩ, makes a magnetic field that a Hall IC on the low-voltage side turns into a proportional voltage. The field is measured differentially, so a uniform outside field is rejected. An integrated shield keeps capacitive coupling from the conductor off the die, so fast dv/dt on the primary adds little output noise. Sensitivity and zero-current output are trimmed in the factory after packaging; magnetic hysteresis is close to zero.

Pins 1 to 8 (the current path) are galvanically separated from pins 9 to 16 (the sensor), so the part can sit on a high-side conductor without a differential amplifier. Certified to UL 60950-1 (ed. 2): 3.6 kVRMS dielectric strength, 616 VRMS basic-isolation working voltage; CB certificate US-23711-A2-UL.

ACS732 runs from 5 V and ACS733 from 3.3 V. Bidirectional (AB) variants sit at 0.5 × VCC with no current (1.65 V at VCC = 3.3 V); unidirectional (AU) variants sit at 0.1 × VCC. The output is ratiometric. The parts are AEC-Q100 qualified, the leadframe is 100 % matte tin for lead-free assembly, and every part is calibrated before shipment.
Internal small-signal bandwidth is 1 MHz typical (CL = 220 pF). On the measured frequency response the -3 dB point is near 1.8 MHz.

Response time: from the input current reaching 90 % of its final value to the output reaching 90 % of full scale. Propagation delay: from the input current reaching 20 % of full scale to the output reaching 20 % of full scale. Rise time: the output going from 10 % to 90 % of full scale. Output slew rate: the output's rate of change, in V/µs, over that same 10 % to 90 % span.

A fault occurs when the size of IP goes past IFAULT, which is user-set between 50 % and 200 % of IPR(MAX); on bidirectional parts both polarities trip it. tRESPONSE(F) runs from IP crossing IFAULT to FAULT falling below VFAULT. FAULT is released once IP drops below IFAULT - IHYST; how fast it then rises depends on RF(PULLUP) and the capacitance on the pin.

A divider from VCC to ground sets the VOC pin between 0.1 × VCC and 0.4 × VCC. Because the divider is ratiometric, the trip current does not move with VCC. Keep the divider resistors under 10 kΩ; with higher values the VOC leakage shifts the trip point.

Sensitivity is the output change for 1 A through the primary, the product of the magnetic coupling (G/A, 1 G = 0.1 mT) and the factory-set amplifier gain (mV/G). Voltage offset error is the departure of the zero-current output from 0.5 × VCC (bidirectional) or 0.1 × VCC (unidirectional) from non-magnetic causes; divide it by Sens to get amperes. Zero-current output spreads with trim resolution and thermal drift.
Zero-current output and sensitivity both scale with VCC: ideally a 5 % rise in VCC gives 5 % more sensitivity. ERAT(SENS) and ERAT(Q) give how far a device departs from that.

Bring the current to the package along the line of the current pins, and keep the trace from reaching in under the middle of the package; a trace run too far under the IC changes the coupling factor and can reduce creepage. If the current has to arrive from the side, keep the angle as small as possible. Do not route other current-carrying phase traces close to or under the IC.

The die heats with current through the sensor, the board and its contacts; the rise depends on layout, copper weight, cooling and the current profile (peak, on-time, duty cycle). The DC self-heating data, taken at TA = 25 °C, shifts to other ambients and also approximates AC and pulsed currents. Surges above the continuous limit are allowed as long as TJ stays under 165 °C. The ASEK73x evaluation board (TED-0001795) has 1500 mm² of 2 oz (0.0694 mm) copper on pins 1 to 4 and on pins 5 to 8, with thermal vias between layers.

The high-isolation board layout has two current pads, each 21.51 mm wide and 17.27 mm tall, one for current in and one for current out, edged with stitching vias to matching copper on the other layers for thermal capacity. The signal-side pad row is 9.54 mm across at 1.27 mm pitch with 0.65 mm pads 2.25 mm long, and stands 7.25 mm clear of the current pads.
